subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu support automatic group-sender agent provisioning, and what identity, authorization, quota/lifecycle, and memory boundaries should become the public contract?
rationale: The code can prove the missing behavior, but choosing the permanent product boundary would affect security, storage, cost, plugin APIs, and multi-user trust semantics.

options.title: Design the generic contract first
options.body: Specify identity-to-agent binding, shared/private memory, lifecycle/quota, authorization, and plugin seams before adding Feishu provisioning.

options.title: Keep explicit routing only
options.body: Continue supporting group session scopes and explicit thread-bound subagents while documenting external deployment patterns for teams that need per-user agents now.

options.title: Decline automatic provisioning
options.body: Close the core request as outside OpenClaw's current trust model and route advanced multi-agent group orchestration to external plugins or deployments.

recommendation.title: Design the generic contract first
recommendation.body: Specify identity-to-agent binding, shared/private memory, lifecycle/quota, authorization, and plugin seams before adding Feishu provisioning.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged work in both Feishu fixes and core subagent thread-binding refactors, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product choice.
